intro_script: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 12th, 2026. We cover 20 key updates, including big news on humanoid robots, the Agility Robotics merger, and drone technology adoption. Stay informed.
outro_script: And that’s all the circuits for today! Thinking about those Apollo humanoids signing their lease – the future is certainly getting more humanoid. Thanks for tuning into your daily dose of robotic revelations. Until tomorrow, keep building!

items.title: GXO Signs Letter of Intent for Up to 1,000 Apptronik Apollo Humanoids
items.summary: GXO Logistics signed a letter of intent with Apptronik to expand trials of the Apollo humanoid robots in its warehouses and establish a commercial rollout framework. If performance and safety targets are met, the companies aim to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids globally over four years, starting in North America in late 2027. The trials will focus on logistics tasks such as goods-to-person picking, case handling, packing, and sortation, assessed against agreed productivity and safety metrics. The commercial deployment is expected to follow a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) structure where GXO pays for the robots. This initiative builds upon prior proof-of-concept work done by both companies.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, GXO signs a letter of intent for up to one thousand Apptronik Apollo humanoids. This agreement establishes a framework for trials and the potential commercial deployment of the humanoid robots within GXO's logistics operations. The collaboration involves testing the Apollo robots in GXO warehouses for logistics tasks including goods-to-person picking, case handling, packing, and sortation, all measured against predefined productivity and safety benchmarks. If performance and safety targets are successfully met, the companies intend to deploy up to one thousand Apollo humanoids globally over a four-year period, commencing in North America in late two thousand twenty-seven. Commercial deployment is projected under a Robotics-as-a-Service structure where GXO assumes the cost of the robots, building upon prior proof-of-concept work. This development indicates a potential pathway for integrating advanced humanoid robotics into large-scale commercial logistics infrastructure.

items.title: Agility Robotics completes merger and secures $465 million in capital ahead of Nasdaq listing
items.summary: Agility Robotics completed a merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, setting the stage for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker symbol AGLT. The transaction is expected to raise approximately $465 million in capital, sourced partly through a PIPE financing led by Foxconn. The capital will fund expansion aimed at increasing the production and commercial adoption of its humanoid robots. The company is expanding commercial operations with existing customers and is preparing for the launch of its next-generation robot, Digit 5. The combined entity focuses on translating its commercial experience into growth while developing manufacturing and software solutions.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Agility Robotics completes a merger and secures four hundred sixty-five million dollars in capital ahead of a Nasdaq listing. This report details the completion of a merger between Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI, which has resulted in a significant capital infusion necessary for future expansion. The transaction was accomplished through a process that included a private investment in public offering financing led by Foxconn, which provided a portion of the capital. This funding is designated to support the expansion of production and the commercial adoption of the company's humanoid robots, along with the preparation for the launch of the next-generation robot, Digit 5. The combined entity is focused on translating commercial experience into growth while developing manufacturing and software solutions. This development signals further movement in the commercialization of advanced robotics within the technology sector.

items.title: Bureau Veritas adopts Nolvis X1 drones for safer ship and offshore inspections
items.summary: Bureau Veritas is utilizing Nolvis X1 drones for remote inspections of hazardous and confined spaces on ships and offshore installations. The X1 is designed to operate in areas inaccessible to personnel, such as ballast tanks, without reliance on satellite navigation. This approach reduces safety risks associated with human entry into these dangerous environments. The system collects visual and spatial data, which is then evaluated by certified marine surveyors. This collaboration supports a shift towards safer, more efficient digital asset management in the maritime industry.

items.title: Cainiao introduces upgraded climbing robot with four-side retrieval and denser storage
items.summary: Cainiao unveiled upgraded climbing robots featuring four-side item retrieval and double-deep storage capabilities. These improvements result in a 15 percent lift efficiency increase and a 20 percent storage density increase. The system also includes a new warehouse planning simulation tool allowing for rapid layout and investment assessment. The robot's movement has been optimized with smoother S-shaped turns, enhancing operational efficiency. The technology is designed for diverse logistics scenarios and has secured international orders.

items.title: Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial
items.summary: Six AGIBOT G2 robots completed 1,730 tasks during a 24-hour trial in a Shanghai convenience store, performing duties like customer assistance and restocking. The work included various activities such as customer interactions, product handling, coffee preparation, and cleaning. The AGIBOT Genie Master framework coordinated the robots, learning from successful and failed attempts to improve performance. Four of the six robots passed the final assessment based on time, task completion, and handling unexpected situations. The trial demonstrated how embodied AI can operate effectively in dynamic, real-world customer-facing environments.

The robots performed a range of duties including customer assistance, product restocking, coffee preparation, and cleaning. The operation was coordinated by the AGIBOT Genie Master framework, which utilized learning from both successful and unsuccessful attempts to refine performance. This trial demonstrated the efficacy of embodied artificial intelligence in dynamic, real-world customer-facing environments. Future developments in embodied AI are expected to focus on expanding practical deployment scenarios for such robotic systems.

items.title: Figure's Night-Shift "Robot Babysitter" Is One of About 30 Jobs Keeping Its Humanoids Running
items.summary: Figure is hiring about 30 people to manage its humanoid robots across various locations and operations. These roles include night-shift coordinators, robot operators, and data operation staff in locations across the US, Brazil, and Mexico. Positions are available for roles in Internal Fleet Operations, Commercial Operations, and Data Operations. Some jobs involve supervising robot maintenance, operating robots, or piloting them to teach new behaviors. The company is staffing these roles to support its vision for 24/7 robot operation and data collection.

items.title: Serve Robotics opens robot delivery network for others to build on
items.summary: Serve Robotics launched the AV Delivery Developer Portal to allow developers, businesses, and AI assistants to programmatically summon its sidewalk delivery robots via an API. This portal provides a sandbox environment for building and testing applications before using live robots. The company aims to open its robot fleet to create affordable and efficient autonomous last-mile delivery solutions for various users. Developers can build applications that request pickups and dropoffs, as Serve handles the complex routing and supervision. The service allows users to build upon the robot fleet to make daily errands more accessible.

items.title: Memories.ai builds standardized egocentric video pipeline
items.summary: Memories.ai builds a standardized pipeline to transform everyday egocentric video into training data for robotics. The company labels footage using models like Memories-H0 for hand pose and EgoAction for actions. It provides a data infrastructure with egocentric video, custom annotation services, and dataset tools for robot learning models. Memories.ai processes and annotates data from partners, focusing on processing their own collected footage rather than wide-ranging collection. The platform aims to be a data-infrastructure partner for robotics and physical AI by tailoring data and potentially expanding into models.

items.title: Niqo Robotics unveils 50-foot AI weeder for large specialty crop farms
items.summary: Niqo Robotics has introduced the RoboWeeder F50, a 50-foot AI weeder designed for large specialty crop farms in North America. This wide-format machine performs three functions simultaneously: precision weeding, thinning, and beneficial spraying. It utilizes Niqo's AI, which rapidly trains algorithms for high accuracy in new crops. The F50 features 14 AI cameras and a 350-nozzle array for highly accurate pinpoint spraying across its width. The robot is tractor-pulled, operates at up to 4.7 mph, and is supported by a local service team.

items.title: FMC³ Robotics introduces Doceo system to help industrial robots learn from factory workers
items.summary: FMC³ Robotics introduced the Doceo system to enable industrial robots to learn manufacturing tasks by observing real-world human factory worker activities. This system collects detailed physical-world data through components like Doceo RealCap, Hub, Cloud, and Driver. The goal is to overcome the challenge of acquiring sufficient data for complex robot training outside of dedicated simulations. The system creates an industrial learning loop connecting task demonstrations with AI model development and robot operation. FMC³ is also developing standardized data infrastructure through collaborations to make industrial training data more consistent and reusable.

items.title: Lincoln Electric introduces XpertLINC to bring physical AI to robotic welding
items.summary: Lincoln Electric introduced XpertLINC, a proprietary physical AI platform integrating vision, motion, and welding expertise. This technology dynamically adjusts robot paths and welding parameters to adapt to real-world conditions, improving productivity and quality. XpertLINC addresses traditional robotic limitations by eliminating the need for extensive programming regarding part fit-up and joint geometry. The system achieves this by scanning parts to assess geometry and utilizing welding experience to set parameters automatically. Initially launched on Cooper welding cobots, XpertLINC aims to optimize manufacturing performance by automating welding intelligence.

items.title: ANYbotics begins deliveries of explosion-proof quadruped robot to industrial customers
items.summary: ANYbotics has started delivering its ANYmal X, a quadruped robot designed for inspection in explosive environments, to industrial customers like Equinor and DSM-Firmenich. This robot is specifically engineered for oil, gas, and chemical facilities where conventional robots are unsuitable due to flammable atmospheres. The ANYmal X incorporates explosion-protection measures, including sealed, nitrogen-filled chambers and flameproof casings for its battery and actuators. It autonomously inspects equipment using visual, thermal, acoustic, and gas sensors to detect faults without facility modifications. The system integrates with maintenance systems, providing end-to-end inspection solutions for hazardous environments.

items.title: Zipline makes drone deliveries quieter with real-time acoustic flight optimization
items.summary: Zipline has implemented sound-optimized dynamic flying using onboard sound modeling to achieve quieter drone deliveries. This optimization has resulted in a 68 percent reduction in overall sound exposure per flight and 24 percent quieter flights at peak volume compared to the 2025 fleet. The drones use real-time wind and altitude data to dynamically adjust their transitions to on-wing flight, mimicking natural flight behaviors. This method also reduces flight times by an average of 53 seconds and decreases energy consumption by 21 percent per flight. This technology allows for even quieter flights and enables future higher-altitude operations.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Zipline makes drone deliveries quieter with real-time acoustic flight optimization. The system employs real-time wind and altitude data to dynamically adjust transitions to on-wing flight, mimicking natural flight behaviors through sophisticated acoustic modeling. This methodology resulted in a sixty-eight percent reduction in overall sound exposure per flight and twenty-four percent quieter flights at peak volume when compared to the twenty twenty five fleet. Furthermore, this optimization reduces flight times by an average of fifty-three seconds and decreases energy consumption by twenty-one percent per flight, allowing for quieter operations and enabling future higher-altitude deployments. This development signals advancements in integrating acoustic awareness with autonomous flight systems across the technology sector.

items.title: Horkos integrates Meltio metal 3D printing technology into new hybrid machining system
items.summary: Horkos and Meltio launched the NX70 Duo version AM, a twin-head non-bed machining center combining metal additive manufacturing and high-precision cutting. This system integrates additive and subtractive manufacturing capabilities within a single machine, allowing for alternating material deposition and machining. Meltio technology uses laser energy and welding wire to precisely deposit metal, enabling complex part production, repair, and prototyping. The hybrid machine addresses manufacturing challenges like labor shortages and space constraints by offering a highly automated solution. This integration supports various industries and builds on existing adoption of Meltio technology in CNC environments.

items.title: CMS brings six-axis Krearob robotic 3D printing system to Formnext 2026
items.summary: CMS will debut its six-axis Krearob robotic large format additive manufacturing (LFAM) system at Formnext 2026 in Frankfurt. This advanced system produces large-scale thermoplastic tooling and components with complex geometries, offering up to 80% material and weight savings. Krearob integrates extrusion, slicing software, and HMI for complete control over the printing process. The system is suitable for demanding aerospace, automotive, and industrial manufacturing applications. CMS will also showcase its Kreator A3 system, which utilizes screw extrusion for large-format printing.

items.title: Melotte reduces weekly 3D printing quality data handling from three hours to 20 minutes with amsight
items.summary: Melotte implemented amsight to streamline the management of additive manufacturing quality data. Previously, gathering and importing this information took approximately three hours weekly. amsight now reduces this data handling time to about 20 minutes per week. This integration allows for much faster root-cause analysis, cutting investigation times from several hours to under 30 minutes. The system connects build, CT, sensor, and maintenance data, creating a traceable quality backbone for demanding industrial markets.

items.title: Welcome, Atlas on Wheels!
items.summary: Atlas on Wheels is a wheeled humanoid research prototype from Boston Dynamics designed to study electric actuator performance through unusual locomotion. It utilizes scooter wheels attached to existing ankle motors to investigate demanding motor behavior while retaining an existing humanoid upper body. The platform possesses capabilities for obstacle avoidance, jumping and landing, and sorting goods, though its overall skill score is low. Standing 190 cm tall and weighing 90 kilograms, it is primarily a research tool focusing on the relationship between mobile navigation, actuator performance, and handling. This prototype represents an experimental configuration of the Atlas robot developed to inform its final design.

items.summary: ESTUN Robotics and RoboDK formed a strategic partnership to integrate their technologies for developing and simulating industrial robotic applications. This collaboration combines ESTUN's robot manufacturing with RoboDK's simulation and offline programming software. The integration has been developed and refined through months of joint technical work, resulting in a satisfactory solution. This alliance aims to simplify robotics adoption in Europe by making automation more accessible through enhanced simulation tools. The partnership seeks to accelerate the delivery of complete, supported robotic solutions for European industry.

items.title: Austrian Space Forum tests robotic rover for 2027 Mars analog mission at Gebrüder Weiss facility
items.summary: The Austrian Space Forum, FH Oberösterreich, and partners tested systems for the AMADEE-27 Mars analog mission at the Gebrüder Weiss facility. A rover developed by the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria was tested to assist the crew with tool transport and navigation on Mars. Gebrüder Weiss will handle the logistics for transporting sensitive research equipment to and from the mission site in Portugal in April 2027. Employees of Gebrüder Weiss gained firsthand experience during the testing by observing the research activities. The mission will involve six analog astronauts conducting experiments in Portugal involving research from multiple international institutions.

items.title: Serve Robotics expands beyond US with DoorDash robot delivery launch in Australia
items.summary: Serve Robotics and DoorDash launched Australia's first footpath robot delivery service in the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct. Customers can opt for robot deliveries from participating restaurants, which travel at walking pace and have remote supervision. The pilot aims to explore how these robots can complement existing delivery options for short, local trips. This initiative supports a broader multi-modal delivery strategy for DoorDash and fosters innovation in the region. The project also involves partnerships with Griffith University for research and opportunities in robotics.
